Ferrari Restoration

By: Etienne Naude | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How an investment in a collectable car could have made you a multi-millionaire.

Summary:
Carlo Viglietti has been working on the restoration of a Ferrari Daytona 365 GTB/4 for over two years. The market for collectable cars has skyrocketed in the last two years, with certain models almost doubling in value. We speak to the restorer of the car and find out about why the market for such cars has risen so sharply.

Further information:
With access to world-renowned car designer Signor Leonardo Fioravanti, we can develop a complete understanding of the origins and history of the Ferrari Daytona - how it was designed, what makes it such a special model, how to make an intelligent investment, and how to preserve the value of the investment by leaving it in the hands of specialists working in South Africa. The insert is about both the economics of investment cars, and a tribute to the highly skilled artisans that dedicate their time and creativity to their preservation.

Press Release:


Ferrari Restoration
For the past two-and-a-half years Carlo Viglietti, one of South Africa’s few certified Ferrari mechanics, has put love, time and energy into restoring a 1969 Daytona model Ferrari belonging to an anonymous private collector. Carte Blanche follows the restoration for over a year and joins Carlo on the track for final tests on this rare specimen. Are cars like this one – now worth one million pounds – the ultimate in recession-proof investments?


Script:


VO
High-performance sports cars have always been desirable status icons, but the market for these cars has gone ballistic over the last two years. Ferraris in particular have become highly sought after, dominating the highest sales prices lists at international car auctions. What’s so special about them?

CARLO VIGLIETTI
It’s a very Italian thing Derek. Italians are very passionate people about most things. A lot of good things come from Italy – design houses and all that. And Ferrari is one of them.

DEREK LINK
The price of a new Ferrari can be like pocket change compared to the vintage Ferraris of the 60s and 70s. But to fetch top dollar they need to be immaculate, and restored to their original condition.

VO
Carlo Viglietti is one of a tiny handful of specialists in South Africa that have had formal training with Ferrari in Maranello, and are certified masters in the art of Ferrari restoration. Restoring a Ferrari is a long labor of love. Carte Blanche first met up with Carlo almost 2 years ago, when he’d just begun work on restoring a 1969 Ferrari Daytona.

CARLO VIGLIETTI
This has been a full bolt-and-nut restoration.

VO
The car was a real diamond-in-the-rough when it first came to the garage. This is what the car looked like when it first came to Pablo Clark. From the color of the body paint to the condition of the seats, it was an almost entirely different vehicle.

CARLO VIGLIETTI
Everything from wiring harness, paintwork, down to metal, wheel bearings, engine rebuild, gearbox rebuild, interior, new carpets, new leather for the dashboard, new leather for the seats.

VO
Paolo Cavalieri is Carlo’s partner at the Ferrari Specialist Pablo Clark garage where this Daytona is being restored.

PAOLO CAVALIERI
Restoration is critically important. It underpins the value. It puts the car in a condition where you can drive it and enjoy it. At the same time there a movement saying that cars that in their original patina have a slightly higher value. The person that restored your car is as important as the restoration itself. So be able to say that the car was restored by Carlo, certified by the factory, really enhances its value.

VO
Taking your vintage Ferrari to Carlo is a little different to your typical car service. On average, it takes him about two years to get a car up to scratch.

DEREK
Carlo, what is involved in a really professional restoration?
CARLO
The most important thing is to stick to the originality of the car. Don’t over-restore the car. Make it look good, like it’s looking now. But don’t go beyond. Don’t chrome things that weren’t chromed at the time. Just make it look like it’s looking now. It’s looking proper.

VO
It’s been a mammoth two a half year restoration on this Daytona. The interiors are practically new; the paint looks as it would’ve when it left the factory in Italy 45 years ago. But the moment of truth lies in how the engine runs.

DEREK
So we going to start it up?
CARLO
It’s a momentous occasion. This has been two and half years.

VO
The restoration is not completely finished here. But the car is out on display because Leonardo Fioravanti is in town. He is the designer of some of Ferrari’s most iconic models, including the Daytona. Signor Fioravanti worked directly for the founder of Ferrari, Enzo Ferrari, the so-called “Commendatore”.

DEREK
Legend has it that you designed the Daytona in 7 days.
LEONARDO FIORAVANTI
Yes, I confirm. In one week. It included Saturday and Sunday, in my home. Immediately Commendatore asked me to make a 1-1 scale model. I was the first to be extremely surprised.

VO
The Daytona, a classic 12 cylinder front engine Ferrari, is one of the highlights of his illustrious career.

DEREK
What makes the Daytona so special?
LEONARDO FIORAVANTI
The first reason is aerodynamics and winning races. The second is very good visibility. Third is the relation between function and aesthetics.
DEREK
All design features have a function?
LEONARDO FIORAVANTI
Yes. If you make aesthetics strictly related with the function, for me that’s the best.

VO
Leonardo is eager to take a look at Carlo’s restoration job. If anyone has a more fastidious eye for detail than Carlo, it’s Leonardo. He spots a tiny deviation from his original design on the front park lights.

DEREK LINK
In 1969 you could have bought a Daytona for around 14 thousand rand.

VO
Today, it will sell for 1 million pounds. At today’s exchange rate, that’s over 21 million rand.

VO
Wayne Plit knows the monetary appreciation of collectable cars as well as anyone. He would have loved to own this Daytona that’s being restored for its new owner in the Western Cape who chooses to remain anonymous, but Wayne will take comfort in his own collection. He has one of the largest collections of cars in South Africa. For him, cars are not only more exciting than traditional investments, but they also perform better.

WAYNE PLIT
It mostly has to do with the fact that people are disappointed with vanilla investments. People are saying I’d rather put my money into classic cars or fine art or coins or stamps. You can establish exactly where classic cars are going versus stocks, for example.
DEREK
You can actually compare it?
WAYNE PLIT
You can in fact overlay on a graph the performance of classic cars as an investment class against the FTSE or the SMP.
DEREK
And right now they are doing pretty well?
WAYNE PLIT
It’s outrageous. Take Ferrari for example. In the last 36 months, about 125% growth. Porsche, 94%. There’s an index called the T-Index, which is everything other than Porsche and Ferrari which are the leaders in classic cars. That’s running at 96%.

DEREK
Now the value of this Daytona has multiplied because of the restoration, hasn’t it?
PAOLO CAVALIERI
Because of the restoration, because of the fact that there are very few in South Africa, and in the world in general. People are moving into phase where they’re realizing that classic motorcars are also pieces of art. But pieces of art that you can enjoy.

VO
To be enjoyed is exactly why Carlo has brought the car to the track.

DEREK
Carlo, after two years and a few hundred hours of work, this is it. The time of testing.
CARLO VIGLIETTI
We’ve come down to crunch time. This horse has been in the stable for too long. It now needs to be exercised.

VO
The car is running like the fastest road car in the world that it once was. It came into the country in 1969. It’s changed ownership 4 times. It’s been perfectly restored. But can it survive Derek Watts taking it for a spin?

DEREK
This wasn’t meant for 2-meter tall people. It was meant for Italians. Okay we can do it.
CARLO VIGLIETTI
Sharp corner! Sharp corner!
DEREK
Do you think I’m improving?
CARLO VIGLIETTI
You’re improving, ja.


DEREK
Carlo, she’s 45 years old and she drives like she’s just out of the showroom.
CARLO VIGLIETTI
It feels good. It feels good to be on the road again with her. She’s loosening up nicely now.
DEREK
It’s the hour of parting. You’ve got to say goodbye.
CARLO VIGLIETTI
That’s going to be a tearful moment.

VO
And so a two and a half year journey comes to an end. But the emotion endures.

CARLO VIGLIETTI
It stirs your passion. It stirs your heart. If you’ve got any blood in you that pumps passion for cars, this is it.
